article_title: Effectiveness of a 5G Local Area Network-Based Digital Microscopy Interactive System: Quasi-Experimental Design.
citation: Xu J, Sha J, Jia S, Li J, Xu L, Shao Z. (2025). Effectiveness of a 5G Local Area Network–Based Digital Microscopy Interactive System: Quasi-Experimental Design. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/70256
title: 5G LAN-based digital microscopy interactive system (DMIS)
description: The DMIS links Panthera I optical microscopes, Motic Digilab 3.0 software, and student computers or mobile devices over a 5G local area network, so it "retains the tactile sensation of physical operation while enabling the display of microscopic images on software-equipped devices." The instructor terminal displays all students' live microscope images in real time, and the software supports four functions—microimage, macroimage, demonstration, and interaction—covering image viewing, video recording, instructor demonstration in forced or unforced mode, file transfer, and text or voice questions.
requirements: Students install the Motic Digilab 3.0 app, connect to the designated 5G LAN, and enter their microscope number to view live images
constraints: When the number of users increases, whether real-time transmission remains stable needs further analysis, per the authors; one student's mobile device was incompatible with the app
target_learners: second-year medical undergraduates in a biology laboratory course
target_learning_goals: knowledge internalization about cell biology specimens
examples: Deployed in Tongji University's second-year biology course across three laboratory sessions, with students working in pairs and submitting reports via Canvas
